`bin/set-config.js` writes exactly one `config.yml` lever per invocation (`--key <lever> --value

## Current State
`plugin/skills/pipeline-smoke-test/SKILL.md` Step 4 (line 71) already cites its verify function with a full call signature in prose — "`bin/lib/smoke-test/verify-claim-race.js`'s `verifyClaimRaceOutcome(attemptRunIds, liveClaim, inProgressLabelCount)` is this verdict's mechanical reference implementation" — matching the established sibling pattern (`composeFixesBlock`, `crossReferenceKeyFiles`), which also cite function name in descriptive prose rather than a literal executable `node -e` shell block (confirmed: neither sibling actually has a literal `node -e` invocation in its skill file either — `pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`'s `composeFixesBlock` citation and `record-creation-subissues.md`'s `crossReferenceKeyFiles(units, grep)` citation are both prose name+signature mentions). Step 6 (line 89), however, cites `verifyCleanupTable`/`renderCleanupTable` by name only, without the call-signature parens Step 4 uses. Neither citation is pinned by a prose-conformance test the way the siblings are: `tests/bundle-fixes-reconciliation-2015.test.js` pins `composeFixesBlock`'s citation (`assert.match(section, /composeFixesBlock/)`), and `tests/specify-decomposition-crossref-prose.test.js` pins `crossReferenceKeyFiles(units, grep)`'s citation and separately asserts the cited module actually exports it. Nothing pins Steps 4/6's citations here, so a rename or removal of either function reference would go undetected.

## Deliverables
- [ ] Add the full call signature to Step 6's `verifyCleanupTable` citation, matching Step 4's style: `verifyCleanupTable(rows)` (and `renderCleanupTable(rows)`, both exported from `bin/lib/smoke-test/verify-cleanup.js`).
- [ ] Add a prose-conformance test (new file, e.g. `tests/pipeline-smoke-test-verify-prose.test.js`) mirroring `tests/specify-decomposition-crossref-prose.test.js`'s pattern: assert Step 4 cites `verifyClaimRaceOutcome(attemptRunIds, liveClaim, inProgressLabelCount)`, assert Step 6 cites `verifyCleanupTable(rows)`, and assert both cited modules actually export those functions (`require('../plugin/bin/lib/smoke-test/verify-claim-race')`/`verify-cleanup`).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `pipeline-smoke-test/SKILL.md` Steps 4 and 6 each cite their verify function with its full call signature in prose (matching the sibling `composeFixesBlock`/`crossReferenceKeyFiles` citation style — a named prose citation, not a literal `node -e` shell block, since neither sibling uses one either).

The raw finding's framing ("siblings have a literal `node -e` invocation snippet") doesn't hold on inspection — neither `composeFixesBlock` nor `crossReferenceKeyFiles` has one; both use a prose name+signature citation pinned by a conformance test. Mirror `specify-decomposition-crossref-prose.test.js`'s two-part pattern (citation-string match + module-export assertion) rather than inventing a new test shape.

## Current State
`plugin/bin/lib/smoke-test/verify-cleanup.js`'s `renderCleanupTable` (line 40) interpolates `row.artifact` directly into a markdown table row with no pipe-character escaping: `` `| ${row.artifact} | ${row.claimed ? 'yes' : 'no'} | ${row.verifiedAbsent ? 'yes' : 'no'} |` `` (line 41). `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js` has a `sanitizeCell` function (line 640, `String(text).replace(/\s+/g, ' ').replace(/\|/g, '\\|').trim()`) built for the identical purpose and already used by that file's own `renderVerifyTable` — but `sanitizeCell` is a private function, not currently in `engine-verify.js`'s `module.exports` (line 656, which lists `runVerify`, `renderVerifyTable`, `resolveArchivedRunDir`, `registerCheck`, `defaultGit`, `defaultGh`, `resolveParent`, `resolvePrNumber` — no `sanitizeCell`). An artifact string containing a literal `|` (e.g. a branch/PR-title-derived description) splits the generated row into extra columns, breaking the Step 6 report table's rendering.

## Deliverables
- [ ] Add `sanitizeCell` to `engine-verify.js`'s `module.exports` (it already exists as a private function; this just makes it importable).
- [ ] In `verify-cleanup.js`, `require('../wrap-up/engine-verify')` and call `sanitizeCell(row.artifact)` before interpolating it into `renderCleanupTable`'s row string.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A test with an artifact string containing a literal `|` renders a well-formed 3-column table row (verify via `renderCleanupTable`'s output split on `|` producing exactly the expected column count for that row).
2. `engine-verify.js`'s own existing tests and usages of `sanitizeCell`/`renderVerifyTable` are unaffected by adding it to `module.exports` (a pure additive export, no signature change).

## Technical Approach
Reuse rather than duplicate: `sanitizeCell` already does exactly what's needed (pipe-escaping plus whitespace collapsing, consistent with how `renderVerifyTable` already sanitizes its own cells), so exporting it and importing it in `verify-cleanup.js` is a two-file, additive-only change — no new escaping logic to write or independently verify.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/smoke-test/verify-cleanup.js` — `renderCleanupTable` (line 40)
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js` — `sanitizeCell` (line 640), `module.exports` (line 656)

## Current State
In `plugin/bin/lib/issues/decomposition-crossref.js`'s `crossReferenceKeyFiles` (line 57), sibling-title matching uses a plain lowercased substring test (`line.toLowerCase().includes(titleLower)`, line 72) with no word-boundary check — a short/generic sibling title can appear as a substring inside an unrelated longer word or phrase in another unit's Gotchas/Prerequisites text, wrongly attaching that unit's grep hits to the wrong sibling's Key Files list. Separately, `extractSection(other.body, 'Gotchas'/'Prerequisites')` (line 68) is recomputed inside the inner `for (const other of list)` loop on every outer `unit` iteration, even though each `other`'s section text doesn't depend on the outer unit — O(N^2) re-parsing for a decomposition batch of N sub-issues — and the injected `grep(ident)` subprocess call (line ~76) has no memoization across outer units sharing the same identifier, real avoidable subprocess-spawn cost that scales with batch size.

## Deliverables
- [ ] Add a word-boundary check to the sibling-title substring match, reusing the existing `escapeRegExp` helper (`plugin/bin/lib/shared-primitives.js`) to build a `\b{escaped title}\b` regex rather than writing a new escaper — the title is user-authored text and may itself contain regex metacharacters.
- [ ] Hoist the `extractSection(other.body, 'Gotchas')` / `extractSection(other.body, 'Prerequisites')` computation for each `other` outside the outer `unit` loop (compute once per `other`, into a map keyed by `other`, not once per unit×other pair).
- [ ] Memoize `grep(ident)` results (a `Map<string, string[]>`) across outer units within one `crossReferenceKeyFiles` call, so the same identifier is grepped at most once per batch regardless of how many units reference it.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A test with a short generic sibling title (e.g. "Fix") that also appears as a substring of an unrelated word in another unit's Gotchas text does not wrongly cross-reference.
2. A test confirms `extractSection` is called at most once per distinct `other` unit within one batch (not once per unit×other pair) — e.g. via a call-counting wrapper or spy on a batch of 3+ units.
3. A test confirms the injected `grep` is called at most once per distinct identifier within one batch, even when multiple units' Gotchas reference the same identifier.
4. All six existing tests in `tests/bin-lib/issues/decomposition-crossref.test.js` pass unchanged.

## Technical Approach
Reuse `escapeRegExp` from `plugin/bin/lib/shared-primitives.js` (already used the same way in `claim-store.js:415` to build a safe dynamic regex from untrusted text) rather than introducing a second escaping implementation. For the two performance fixes, restructure the double loop so the `other`-keyed work (section extraction) happens once per `other` before the outer `unit` loop runs, and thread a shared `Map` for grep memoization through the whole `crossReferenceKeyFiles` call.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/decomposition-crossref.js` — `crossReferenceKeyFiles` (line 57), `extractSection` (line 33), the substring match (line 72), the `grep(ident)` call (line ~76)
- `plugin/bin/lib/shared-primitives.js` — `escapeRegExp` (line 43), to reuse rather than reimplement
- `tests/bin-lib/issues/decomposition-crossref.test.js` — 129 lines, 6 existing tests, all must stay green

## Current State
`package.json`'s `test` script (`"test": "CT_HOOKS_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS=60000 node --test $(find tests tools/upstream-drift/tests -name '*.test.js' | sort)"`) uses two POSIX-only shell constructs: a `VAR=value command` env-prefix, and `$(...)` command substitution to enumerate test files. `npm test` on Windows runs this under `cmd.exe`, which supports neither, so it fails immediately with `'CT_HOOKS_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS' is not recognized as an internal or external command`. `plugin/skills/test/verification.md`'s Step 2 documents `bin/verify.js --cmd tests="npm test"` as this repo's canonical verification invocation; `verify.js` just shells out to whatever string a `--cmd` value carries (`spawnImpl(command, {shell: true})`, `plugin/bin/lib/verify/run.js:41`), so it inherits the failure unchanged rather than causing it. (The original request's claim that this exact failure was "already documented in this project's own memory notes" doesn't hold — no repo doc, `docs/incident-log.md`, or session memory records this specific pairing; related but distinct Windows-portability incidents exist, e.g. a path-backslash-in-string-literal bug `[IL-154]`.)

## Deliverables
- [ ] A small portable Node script (e.g. `tools/run-tests.js`) that: walks `tests/` and `tools/upstream-drift/tests/` for `*.test.js` files in JS (no shell glob), matching today's `find tests tools/upstream-drift/tests -name '*.test.js' | sort` output exactly; sets `process.env.CT_HOOKS_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS = process.env.CT_HOOKS_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS || '60000'` before spawning; spawns `node --test <files>` with `stdio: 'inherit'` and exits with the child's exit code.
- [ ] `package.json`'s `test` script updated to `"node tools/run-tests.js"` (or equivalent), removing the env-prefix and `$(...)` constructs entirely — fixing the shell portability at the source, so `verification.md`'s documented `--cmd tests="npm test"` invocation needs no Windows-specific alternative and stays unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The new script's resolved file list is identical (same set, no additions or omissions) to `find tests tools/upstream-drift/tests -name '*.test.js' | sort`'s current output (549 files as of this writing) — verify by diffing the two lists.
2. `npm test`'s underlying invocation contains neither a POSIX env-prefix (`VAR=value cmd`) nor `$(...)` command substitution (verified by inspection; a live `cmd.exe` run isn't available on this build's host, so this AC is a code-shape check, not an on-host proof).
3. `CT_HOOKS_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS` still resolves to `60000` during `npm test` when the caller hasn't set it (unchanged from today — `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-exec.js`'s `resolveTimeout` reads it via `process.env`).
4. `npm test` still passes in full on this (POSIX) host after the change.

## Technical Approach
Fix the shell-portability problem once at its source (`package.json`'s script) rather than teaching every consumer — `verify.js`'s documented example, any human running `npm test` directly — a Windows-specific workaround. `CT_HOOKS_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS`'s default is a widen-for-tests override, not a correctness requirement: `resolveTimeout` (`git-exec.js`) already falls back to `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` when the env var is unset or non-numeric, so even a script bug that failed to set it would degrade to today's production timeout rather than break test execution outright — the script should still set it, though, to keep parity with today's wider test-only timeout.

### Key Files
- `package.json` — the `test` script (line 7)
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-exec.js` — `resolveTimeout` (line ~50), confirms the env var has a safe fallback
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/run.js:41` — confirms `verify.js` just shells out to the `--cmd` string unchanged, so no separate `verify.js` fix is needed once `npm test` itself is portable

## Gotchas
- `docs/incident-log.md:421` documents a precedent directly on point: a prior change to `package.json`'s test-file enumeration silently dropped a whole new module's tests from `npm test` without any red signal — "the suite gets quieter, not redder." AC1's exact-diff check exists specifically to catch that failure mode here.
- No live Windows/`cmd.exe` host is available in this environment to run AC2 end-to-end; it is verified by removing the two named incompatible shell constructs, not by an on-host pass.

## Original request
`# Reflect — staged finding 1`

**Category:** tangential

Origin: reflect light mode from #1965 (wrap-up Phase 1)
Defer-reason: tangential

On this Windows box, invoking the documented `verify.js` command exactly as written fails immediately: `report.json`'s `tests` check exits non-zero with `'CT_HOOKS_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS' is not recognized as an internal or external command, operable program or batch file.` — because `npm test`'s own script uses POSIX env-prefix syntax that `npm` runs under `cmd.exe` on Windows, which rejects it.

## Current State
`plugin/bin/lib/ports/ensure.js`'s `ensure()` reads and parses `.env.local`'s managed region twice on the path that matters most: an existing lease whose bound port is not free (the common case at every subsequent session start against an already-running dev server). It reads once unconditionally as `regionBefore` (line ~70), then `isRegionCurrent()` (line 34) re-reads and re-parses the same unmodified file itself at line 90, with no write between the two reads.

## Deliverables
- [ ] Extract a `regionIsCurrent(region, base, leaseServices, policyServices)` helper that takes an already-parsed region array (the `readManagedRegion()` return value) instead of a checkout path, containing today's `isRegionCurrent` comparison logic (PORT match + `sameServices`).
- [ ] Keep `isRegionCurrent(checkoutRoot, base, leaseServices, policyServices)` exported with its current signature and behavior, reimplemented as a thin wrapper: read `.env.local`, parse it, delegate to `regionIsCurrent`.
- [ ] In `ensure()`, replace the `isRegionCurrent(checkoutRoot, base, lease.services, policyServices)` call with `regionIsCurrent(regionBefore, base, lease.services, policyServices)`, reusing the region already read into `regionBefore`.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `ensure()` reads `.env.local` at most once per invocation for the managed-region check (verify via a spy/count on `fs.readFileSync` in a test exercising the existing-lease-not-free branch).
2. Existing `tests/bin-lib/ports/ensure.test.js` assertions pass unchanged — `isRegionCurrent`'s signature and behavior (checkout-root-in, boolean-out) are untouched, only its internals delegate.

## Technical Approach
Keeping `isRegionCurrent`'s public signature intact is required, not optional: it's exported (`module.exports`) and five assertions in `tests/bin-lib/ports/ensure.test.js` (lines 121, 181, 184, 187, 188) call it directly as `isRegionCurrent(dir, base, leaseServices, policyServices)` against a checkout path. Changing that signature to take a pre-parsed region would fail AC2. The fix instead splits the comparison logic out into a new `regionIsCurrent(region, ...)` that both `isRegionCurrent` (file-reading wrapper, for the standalone tests and any other caller) and `ensure()` (already holding `regionBefore`) can call — only `ensure()`'s internal call site changes.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/ports/ensure.js` — `isRegionCurrent` (line 34), `regionBefore` read (line ~70), the call site at line 90 to redirect
- `tests/bin-lib/ports/ensure.test.js` — existing `isRegionCurrent` assertions that must keep passing unchanged; no new test required by the ACs beyond the read-count check in AC1, but the existing-lease-not-free branch (`stillFree` false, `isRegionCurrent`-equivalent true) should be the one exercised

## Gotchas
- `isRegionCurrent`'s own missing-file branch returns `false` before ever calling `readManagedRegion` — `regionIsCurrent` must treat a `null`/falsy `region` argument the same way (`if (!region) return false;`), matching `readManagedRegion`'s existing `if (!region) return false;` check inside the current function body.
- The two reads only both happen on one branch (existing lease AND port not free) — `!existingEntry` and `existingEntry && stillFree` never call `isRegionCurrent` at all today, so this is a hot-path optimization for the "server already running" case, not a fix that touches every call.

Surface: infra

## Current State
`plugin/bin/lib/timing/derive.js` attributes a `skill_invoked` event to a phase by name: a `claude-tweaks:*` skill that is one of the ten `PHASES` opens that phase, a skill listed in `NESTED_PARENT` (`simplify`, `reflect`, `visual-review`, `capture`, `design-wrapper`, `challenge`, `assess-agent-autonomy`, `ledger`, `journeys`, all mapped to `'enclosing'`) attributes to the phase that is already open, and — by the file's own comment — "an un-mapped `claude-tweaks:*` skill_invoked event opens a new top-level phase named after the skill", so that "a maintainer adding a new nested-skill call site inside review/wrap-up/build must add its name here, or every run will grow a spurious top-level phase." Nothing enforces that sentence. The only test touching the roster is `tests/bin-lib/timing/derive.test.js`'s `NESTED_PARENT.journeys === 'enclosing'` pin. The sibling roster for ceremony skip tags is pinned by `tests/ceremony-profile-roster.test.js`, which walks `plugin/skills/**` and asserts every fast-lane skip mention in the corpus carries a rostered tag — the shape this record asks for.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `tests/timing-nested-parent-roster.test.js`: walks the phase-skill directories (`build`, `test`, `review`, `design-wrapper`, `wrap-up`, `flow`, and their `_shared/` contracts) and collects every `/claude-tweaks:{name}` invocation that appears *outside* a `## Next Actions` block (Next Actions lines are human launchers, not nested Skill-tool calls) and outside fenced code blocks that render commands for a human; each collected `{name}` must be a `PHASES` member, a `NESTED_PARENT` key, or on a small, commented allowlist of skills that are named descriptively but never invoked from a phase (e.g. `specify` cited as the upstream, `sweep` as the orchestrator). The assertion message names the file, line, and skill so the fix is one roster entry.
- [ ] A second assertion in the same file: every `NESTED_PARENT` key is invoked somewhere in that scan, so a stale entry (a nested skill that no phase skill calls any more) is reported rather than carried forever.
- [ ] A comment on `NESTED_PARENT` pointing at the test by name, replacing the "must add its name here" sentence's implicit trust with the explicit pin.
- [ ] The existing `derive.test.js` pin stays; `npm test` picks the new file up via the recursive glob (no registration).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Deleting any current `NESTED_PARENT` key makes the new test fail naming a real call site in the corpus (each of the nine keys is exercised).
2. Adding a `/claude-tweaks:{new}` invocation inside a phase skill's step body without a roster entry makes the test fail with file, line, and skill name; adding the entry makes it pass.
3. A `/claude-tweaks:{name}` under a `## Next Actions` heading or inside a human-facing fenced command block does not trip the test.
4. The test passes on the current corpus; `npm test` is green.

## Technical Approach
Scan the corpus the way the ceremony roster test does (walk `plugin/skills`, read each file, regex per line) rather than parsing `docs/skill-graph.md`: the graph rows are prose and describe every relationship kind, while the timing roster cares only about what a phase skill *invokes* mid-phase, which is exactly what the phase directories' step bodies say. The `## Next Actions` exclusion is the load-bearing heuristic — every phase skill ends with a launcher block naming skills it does not invoke — so the scanner tracks the current `##` heading while walking lines. The stale-key assertion is the half the ceremony test lacks and the cheap half to add, since the scan already produces the invoked set.

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/timing/derive.js` — `PHASES`, `NESTED_PARENT`, `isTopLevel`, the roster comment.
- `tests/ceremony-profile-roster.test.js` — the corpus-walk template (`walk`, per-line regex, heading tracking).
- `tests/bin-lib/timing/derive.test.js` — existing pin (unchanged).
- `plugin/skills/{build,test,review,design-wrapper,wrap-up,flow}/**` and `plugin/skills/_shared/**` — the scanned corpus.

## Gotchas
- `skill_invoked` events exist only for model-initiated Skill calls, so a skill a phase names only in prose ("see `/claude-tweaks:specify`") never produces an event; that is why the scan needs an allowlist for descriptive mentions and why the allowlist must stay short and commented — a growing allowlist is the roster problem moved.
- `PHASES` names (`test`, `review`, `polish`, `wrap-up`) are themselves skills invoked by `/flow`; they are top-level by design and must be excluded from the nested check, not added to `NESTED_PARENT`.
- `design-wrapper` is invoked as the `polish` phase by `/flow` (top-level there) and as a nested call from `/review` (Step 3.8 craft critics); `NESTED_PARENT` maps it to `'enclosing'` and `derive.js` resolves the polish phase separately — the test asserts roster membership only, never phase semantics.
- Keep the scan to the phase directories; `backlog`, `tidy`, and `sweep` invoke many skills but never run inside a timed pipeline phase.

Origin: reflect light from #1143
Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`skills/review/SKILL.md`'s Overview states: "When invoked by `/claude-tweaks:flow`, review runs in **full** mode by default (code + visual)." But the Input resolution section's actual mode-selection rules (1-8) are purely token-based — the literal word `full` appearing in `$ARGUMENTS` is the only thing that selects full mode. There is no rule that checks `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` (or any other flow-context signal) and defaults to full mode when no explicit mode token is present. A flow executor who invokes `/claude-tweaks:review {spec}` without typing `full` explicitly silently gets **code** mode instead — no warning, no divergence from the documented default surfaced anywhere. This run (#1143's own flow continuation) hit exactly this gap: `/claude-tweaks:review #1143` was invoked without the `full` token, resolving to code mode per the skill's own Input resolution rule 1. No actual harm occurred this run (the record's `surface: backend`, so visual review would have been skipped by Step 6's own detection regardless of mode) — but on a frontend record, the same omission would silently skip the browser visual-review pass in a context where the skill's own documentation promises it always runs.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Add a rule to `skills/review/SKILL.md`'s Input resolution (or its own note) that defaults to full mode when `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` is set (or an equivalent flow-context signal is present) and no explicit mode token (`full`/`visual`/`journey:`/`discover`) appears in `$ARGUMENTS` — making the documented "flow invokes review in full mode by default" promise self-enforcing rather than dependent on the flow executor remembering to type `full`.
- [ ] Audit `skills/flow/SKILL.md`'s own Step 4 invocation prose for the same gap — it also just says "Flow invokes `/claude-tweaks:review` in full mode by default" without specifying the mechanism that makes this true.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `/claude-tweaks:review {spec}` invoked with `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` set and no explicit mode token resolves to full mode (verifiable by reading the updated Input resolution rule).
2. `/claude-tweaks:review {spec}` invoked standalone (no `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`) and no explicit mode token still resolves to code mode, unchanged — the fix must not alter standalone behavior.
3. An explicit mode token (`full`/`visual`/`journey:`/`discover`) still always wins over the flow-context default, in either context.

**Related:** #1634

**CLAUDE.md:** CLAUDE | **Section:** Auto-Mode Contract + Bookend Architecture (v4.6+) | **Category:** drift | **Classification:** additive | **Confidence:** high

Verified-as-of: b3962148502d70e2970b7591c55634d62dc74162

## Current State

`plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-contract.md` line 30 states verbatim: "Begin stop is opt-in under `auto`. `/flow` defaults to `auto`, and in `auto` the Manifesto renders as a **read-only FYI** ... so the everyday auto pipeline has effectively **one** user-facing stop ... The 'at most two stops' promise is a ceiling, not a floor." CLAUDE.md's own paragraph omits this distinction entirely, leaving a reader (or an agent acting on CLAUDE.md alone) to assume the Manifesto is normally an interactive stop in default `auto`, which it is not.

## Deliverables

**Current:**
```
claude-tweaks pipelines have at most two stops in `auto` mode: a **Pipeline Config Manifesto** at the start (one structured numbered-options block collecting all policy levers in a single message) and a **Wrap-Up Review Console** at the end (one batch table consolidating everything auto-decided or staged). Everything in between is policy-driven automation logged to the auto-decision log.
```

**Proposed:**
```
claude-tweaks pipelines have at most two stops in `auto` mode: a **Pipeline Config Manifesto** at the start (one structured numbered-options block collecting all policy levers in a single message) and a **Wrap-Up Review Console** at the end (one batch table consolidating everything auto-decided or staged). The two-stop ceiling isn't a floor: in default `auto`, the Manifesto renders as a **read-only FYI** (displays levers, doesn't gate), so the everyday run has effectively **one** user-facing stop — the end Review Console. Pass `confirm` (or `hybrid`) to turn the Manifesto into a real approval gate. Everything in between is policy-driven automation logged to the auto-decision log.
```

## Acceptance Criteria

CLAUDE.md's Auto-Mode Contract paragraph presents "at most two stops" as if both stops normally occur in `auto` mode, but the canonical `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-contract.md` (the file this paragraph cites as single source of truth) now explicitly clarifies that the ceiling is not a floor: in default `auto`, the Manifesto renders as a read-only FYI and never gates, so the everyday auto run has effectively only one user-facing stop (the end Review Console) — the Manifesto only becomes a real stop under `confirm`/`hybrid`.

Refs #68. `skills/routine/create-and-update.md` now sets `notifications` unconditionally on the direct-create path (Step 6 body template), documents the field, and adds a Step 7 preview line stating a routine emails on every firing — all implemented and pinned by `tests/routine-notifications.test.js`. Step 8's guided-creation branch was also extended with a follow-up `RemoteTrigger {action: "update", trigger_id, body: {notifications: {...}}}` call, but its correctness for the `notifications` field specifically is unconfirmed: Task 0's empirical premise-check (does `RemoteTrigger update` actually persist `notifications` the same way `create` was already confirmed live) requires the `RemoteTrigger` tool, which was unavailable in both the original build session and this ledger-resolution session (`ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` returns no match in either).

**Shaping-time fact-check (2026-08-23):** the `RemoteTrigger` tool, previously unavailable in both prior sessions, is now available in this session (`ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` resolves it) — the same finding as sibling record #1302, filed from the same ledger-resolution pass. This shaping session did **not** attempt Task 0's actual premise-check: creating a throwaway routine via `RemoteTrigger` and confirming `notifications` persists is a real external-service mutation with no delete API to clean it up afterward (per the record's own Deliverables), which is build-time work requiring the build session's own judgment and authorization, not something to run speculatively during shaping. The build session should re-verify `RemoteTrigger` availability in its own environment before assuming this blocker is fully resolved — tool availability may be session-type-dependent (interactive vs. cloud/routine).

- If Task 0 found the `update` mechanism does not work as assumed, `create-and-update.md` Step 8 is corrected and `tests/routine-notifications.test.js` (or a new test) pins the corrected behavior.

### Key Files
